lead: Bitcoin / BTC-USD — The exchange king falls, the ETF dream stands
smaller: Nvidia / NVDA — Revenue triples, the bar moves again
Palantir / PLTR — Spy-tech wins the NHS, sellers win the day
Ross Stores / ROST — Black Friday belongs to the bargain bin
why_lead: Bitcoin fell 4.44% to 35,813.81 USD on the 2023-11-21 daily close, with Solana -8.02%, Dogecoin -7.40%, XRP -5.28% and ether -4.21%, on newly published criminal charges at Binance (n1144) and its founder's exit (n1149, n1148), plus Bittrex's shutdown (n1145) and a suit against Tether's bank partner (n1147). It is the day's biggest crowd story with a simple fork (cleanup before ETFs versus another exchange unwind). Social signal from BONK's 2,300% run (n1142), SOL-versus-XRP chatter (n1135) and Argentina demand (n2268); analog is FTX, named by own-date headlines (n1124, n1118, n1140) with the mechanism (run versus governance shock); smart money split between momentum/ETF bulls (n1913, n1112, n1103, n1928) and plumbing skeptics; breaks on the 20-session reference, Solana's slide, delistings (n1131) and ETF timing.
why_smaller: Nvidia: material update of the 2023-11-21 lead with newly published results (n1060, n1332, n1333) published after the US close on 2023-11-21, before the cutoff; kept brief and secondary because the theme led yesterday. Pre-release close 499.44 USD (-0.92%, +14.39% over 20 sessions); the buy-regardless crowd (n0190) and Bloomberg's great-is-good-enough test (n1315) plus China risk (n0927, n0501) supply the break.

Palantir: a concrete contract catalyst (NHS deal worth up to GBP 480 million, n1062, n1089) met a 7.22% drop to 19.80 USD after a run toward a two-year high (n0746): a sell-the-news narrative distinct from Nvidia's earnings test, with privacy and Gaza-linked backlash (n1063, n1343) as the break.

Ross Stores: the off-price trade-down into Black Friday (n1002, n0619, n0764, n0845), +12.87% over 20 sessions to 130.72 USD; Lowe's cut (n1324, -3.12%), Nordstrom's miss (n1335), TJX's holiday guidance cut (n0430) and mixed consumer signals (n2066) supply the break.
